verdict.rationale: Galileo's docs host a Mintlify API reference generated from its published OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec (202 /v2/ paths). Every endpoint has a "Try it" playground that executes real requests, so the reference is interactive and its examples are runnable. The probe 404s on docs-origin OpenAPI paths do not contradict this, because the spec is served from the API origin. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the playground, a sandbox or test environment (it runs against production with a real token), and clean spec metadata (title "FastAPI", version "0.1.0").

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The Mintlify-hosted API reference (generated from the OpenAPI document) runs the "Try it" playground per endpoint, with .md mirrors of every page.
The runner mounts client-side and executes against the production API with a real token.
Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document at its API origin (202 paths, all under /v2/)
